Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

lack verb and noun

also be lacking, be without, do without, go without, shortage, lack of, be missing, be short of

classical

Ov. Met. 6.354: caret ōs ūmōre loquentis
Liv. 3.29.2: carēbis … praedae parte, mīles

careō, carēre, caruī, caritūrus

verb, second conjugation: with the ablative

lack, be without, go without

Cicero defines it: carēre igitur hoc significat: egēre eō quod habēre velīs, to lack means to be without what you would like to have (Tusc. 1.88). Also of what one is well without: caret perīclō, he runs no risk (Publil. Sent. C 32).

Examples

  • Semper cōnsilium tunc deest, cum opus est maximē.

    Good advice is always lacking just when it is needed most.Publil. Sent. S 31

  • Inopiae dēsunt multa, avāritiae omnia.

    Poverty lacks many things; greed lacks everything.Publil. Sent. I 7

  • caret ōs ūmōre loquentis et faucēs ārent, vixque est via vōcis in illīs

    my mouth lacks moisture as I speak, my throat is parched, and my voice can hardly get throughOv. Met. 6.354–355

  • Quod tibi plānē deest, mī fīlī, nōn est ingenium sed ambitiō!

    What you plainly lack, my son, is not talent but ambition!Traupman 162

Other words

  • inopia, inopiae f. — lack, shortage, want

    noun, first declension · classical · Liv. 5.47.4: in summā inopiā cibī; Publil. Sent. I 7: inopiae dēsunt multa

    The noun: a lack of something, with the genitive; also poverty.

  • dēsum, deesse, dēfuī — be lacking, be missing

    verb, irregular: what is lacking is the subject, the person who lacks it in the dative · also used · classical · Publil. Sent. S 31: semper cōnsilium tunc deest, cum opus est maximē; Traupman 162: quod tibi plānē deest

  • dēficiō, dēficere, dēfēcī, dēfectum — run short, fail (someone)

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 1.11.30: animus sī tē nōn dēficit aequus

    Of what gives out: strength, time, supplies, courage.

  • egeō, egēre, eguī — be in want of, need

    verb, second conjugation: with the ablative (or the genitive) · also used · classical · Gell. 13.24.1: sī nōn est, egeō

    Lacking what one needs; see require.

See also require, poor, enough.
